page: Microsoft Azure E2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a 77 GB local SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2701.48, while the single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds fall within the average range. However, multi-core performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also a bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 140.21 GB/sec, and uncached large-block read and write speeds ranking in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ads_v5 offers a high memory density relative to its low vCPU count, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. However, users face significant performance tradeoffs in compute-intensive and database operations. Passmark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all rank in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight database caching, basic text processing, or memory-heavy, single-threaded applications rather than high-throughput web serving, complex compilation, or parallelized data science tasks.

It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 8.0 GB per core ratio, alongside a bundled 77 GB local SSD. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top 25%, but reveal weak multi-core performance and poor memory bandwidth. Database operations, static web serving, and software compilation also score in the bottom 10% to 25%. This qualitative resource profile makes the E2ads_v5 cost-efficient for memory-intensive, low-compute tasks. It is best suited for lightweight memory-bound applications, basic text processing, and single-threaded workloads rather than high-throughput databases or parallel processing.
